conventions.convention: The smooth Godbillon–Vey convention is dω = η ∧ ω and GV(F) = [η ∧ dη] in real de Rham cohomology. No integral refinement is defined.
Bott vanishing assumes full AC and concludes vanishing only for real Pontryagin monomials of cohomological degree greater than 2q, equivalently invariant-polynomial degree k > q.

Relative characteristic-disk genericity assumes a C² atlas and a supplied nowhere-vanishing C² defining form. The leafwise boundary adjustment asserts arbitrary C⁰ closeness, not arbitrary C¹ or C² closeness.
A C² first-integral annulus has a C² leaf product, but a C¹ tangent generator has only a positive C¹ speed a(s,θ). Neither θ-independent speed nor a C² flow of that generator is asserted.
The finite surface normal forms are homeomorphism normal forms. Their statement does not provide differentiable smoothing or C² parametrizations from standard disks.
Exact cap-collar matching requires the same fixed smooth positive transverse field and the same short orbit segments. The product interval is fixed before checking the actual collar section range.

Ordinary one-sided limit cycles are nonidentity classes in π₁/N_j. Limitwise-nullhomotopy classes instead form the normal subgroup Π₁ʲ ⊆ N_j; their nearby displacements are null for every sufficiently small positive parameter, with no uniform cap bound.
The loop product traverses the first loop first. Forward holonomy is an antihomomorphism; the representation is ρ([a]) = h_(a⁻¹).

The finite module-model theorem unconditionally supplies an exact fully faithful essentially surjective functor. A specified quasi-inverse additionally requires supplied splitting data; objectwise finite presentations do not select them simultaneously.

Modules are left modules, A = End(P)ᵒᵖ, and a kernel from A to B is a (B,A)-bimodule. Its two k-scalar actions agree. Finite functor-category assertions use the explicitly supplied set of allowed finite-dimensional vector-space structures.
Internal shifts satisfy (X{r})_d = X_(d−r), strictly compose by addition, and introduce no signs. The cochain shift [1] instead lowers placement and negates the differential.
Shift compatibility is supplied data θ_(X,r): F(X{r}) → F(X){r}, with unit and cocycle. Transformations must satisfy θᴳ_(X,r)η_(X{r}) = (η_X{r})θᶠ_(X,r).

load_bearing.statement: For a C¹ Euclidean field on an open set, the unique maximal flow is jointly C¹, has C¹ regular-point flow boxes, and satisfies the stated variational equation. A C² field has jointly C² flow and flow boxes with the stated second variation. Individual C¹-field trajectories are C² in time; a trajectory remaining in a compact subset of the domain has no finite maximal endpoint. These conclusions use no full AC or DC.

Assume ACω. For an oriented Hausdorff boundaryless C² surface, possibly disconnected: compact subsets lie inside compact finitely cellulated C² subsurfaces; compact connected subsurfaces have the stated oriented topological genus normal forms and group calculations; every component has torsion-free fundamental group; every regular embedded C² nullhomotopic circle bounds an embedded compact C² disk region, unique unless its ambient connected component is a sphere, where there are two.

Assume ACω. A compact C² leafwise disk cap, a fixed smooth positive transverse field near its entire image, and finite holonomy-trivial continuation of a fixed positive C² transversal give a uniform interval J and a jointly C² product P with central cap B, leaf-valued slices, positive transverse tracks and dP⁻¹(TF) = ker(dt). Exact collar matching additionally requires the transported section to lie in J and its trace points to use the same short V-orbit segments.

Under ACω, for the stated C² atlas, supplied C² defining form and C² disk map: a transverse boundary has a zero-free collar; a leafwise boundary admits a boundary-fixed collar adjustment with arbitrary C⁰ closeness; once a fixed collar is zero-free, arbitrarily small C² perturbations fixed near it give finitely many interior nondegenerate center/saddle singularities. Distinct singular ambient leaves are not asserted.

Assume ACω. A nonempty connected open planar set with a C² first-integral atlas and simple compact C² circle leaves whose Jordan domains are strictly nested and consistently oriented is an open annulus with an increasing C² leaf product. A nowhere-zero C¹ tangent generator has positive C¹ coefficient a(s,θ), without a θ-independent or C² speed assertion.

Assume ACω. For a C² codimension-one foliation and a C² trace annulus with leafwise loops and transverse point tracks, a compact continuous leafwise nullhomotopy at s₀ implies leafwise nullhomotopy for every s in some open interval about s₀.

Under ACω, a generic C² immersed finite-double-point representative of a nonidentity limitwise-nullhomotopy class admits a short one-field leaf-synchronized fence. Intrinsic compact leaf sets contained in the field domain are separated from their short nonzero field displacements. All actual level collisions use one fixed finite set of eligible source pairs; eligible collisions need not persist at every height, and cuts decrease rank only when the subloops close on their actual common interval.

Assume ACω. A relative generic characteristic disk with closed transverse boundary and distinct singular images in distinct ambient leaves has an inclusion-minimal simple regular or homoclinic characteristic cycle with nonidentity ambient holonomy. Its bounded source domain minimizes area among such cycles. Minimum selection alone does not assert inward identity at a three-sector homoclinic cycle.

For an intrinsic finite k-linear abelian category with the stated chosen simple representatives and projective covers, P is their sum and A = End(P)ᵒᵖ is finite-dimensional. H = C(P,−) is k-linear, exact, fully faithful and objectwise essentially surjective onto finite-dimensional left A-modules. Supplied splitting data additionally give a specified k-linear equivalence; such equivalences transfer intrinsic finiteness. The unconditional objectwise construction uses finite choices and does not supply simultaneous splitting.

With the stated agreeing scalar and set-sized conventions, for finite-dimensional unital k-algebras A,B: finite (B,A)-bimodules give k-linear right exact tensor functors on finite left modules; every k-linear right exact functor is canonically naturally isomorphic to F(A) ⊗_A −; all natural transformations of tensor functors correspond to bimodule maps. These assignments give an equivalence, without an infinite-coproduct hypothesis, commutativity or choice.

For a k-linear coherently shift-compatible F on graded left modules over graded k-algebras, M = F(A) becomes a graded (B,A)-bimodule by m·a = F(r_a)θ⁻¹_(A,d)(m) for homogeneous a ∈ A_d and r_a: A{d} → A. The supplied cocycle and naturality give associativity, commuting actions and agreeing central scalars. Degree-zero endomorphisms alone recover only A₀.

For a field k and graded k-algebras A,B, graded (B,A)-bimodules with degree-zero maps are equivalent as k-linear categories to k-linear right exact coproduct-preserving coherently shift-compatible functors GrMod₀(A) → GrMod₀(B), with coherent transformations. Evaluation at A with reconstructed action is a quasi-inverse, the comparison is a coherent natural isomorphism, and the unit and comparison satisfy the triangle identities. No commutativity beyond k or choice is used.

concerns.concern: Its Statement permits an arbitrary oriented Hausdorff C² surface S without second countability. F1 cites the cellulation supplier, whose Statement requires the ambient surface to be second-countable. Proof 1.1 already uses finitely many chart neighborhoods around the relevant compact set, but does not explicitly restrict the ambient surface to their second-countable open union before applying F1.

Proof 9.1 invokes F3 to obtain a field Y that 'equals X and DX on Γ'. The drift supplier's Statement asserts Y = X on Γ, not DY = DX there. Its Proof 3.1 does establish zero derivative for the added drift, so the needed stronger interface is recoverable from that proof but is absent from the quoted proposition.

alerts.finding: Proof 1.1 concludes 'The module P is projective by [L1]'. L1 states only 'Projective modules are direct summands of free modules'. The opened characterization theorem qualifies the unrestricted converse by AC. Here P is a summand of finite free A^r, so the finite-basis lifting argument is available, but that reverse implication is not the cited L1 assertion.

Proof 1.1 first says 'Choose one smooth positively transverse field V near the compact image of Γ', then enlarges the leafwise cap to B: ŵW → L and says 'Apply [F3] with the same V on this fixed cap'. The cited cap-product suppliers require V on a neighborhood of the entire B(ŵW). No extension retaining the original V near Γ is stated, and the cap interior need not lie in that original field domain.

Proof 2.1 chooses V only 'near the compact image of Γ' and constructs an enlarged cap B; Proof 3.1 then applies the fixed-cap product 'to B with this same field V'. The opened product supplier requires V near the whole compact cap image. The proof does not state the needed extension of V over that image while retaining it near the projection collar.

F2 describes the supplier as saying nullhomotopy 'persists ... while the deformation is compact'. The supplier actually concludes persistence only on some open parameter interval about the specified null loop. Proof 3.1 and this consumer's conclusion use sufficiently nearby loops, so the mathematical application is local, but the cited fact omits that essential locality.

F1 attributes to 'lem-characteristic-disk-center-saddle-index-count' the 'index count with one more center than saddle in a one-quadrant inner disk'. That source assumes a characteristic covector nonzero on the boundary and an everywhere-leafwise or everywhere-transverse boundary. A homoclinic boundary contains its saddle and does not meet those premises. The separate 'lem-one-quadrant-homoclinic-disk-has-one-more-interior-center-than-saddle' states the strict-interior count, and the consumer's F2 route reaches it, but F1 names the wrong proposition for this clause.

seams_checked.note: Uses preserve intrinsic leafwise homotopy, endpoint transversals and the reversed-loop representation. C² adaptations reproduce finite-chart arguments rather than asserting that smooth germ statements automatically apply unchanged.

The countable-choice definition, C¹ atlas/holonomy clauses and compact one-manifold classification retain their qualifications. The mapping-torus example uses the circle-fibration clause and does not replace its inverse-monodromy convention.

End(P)ᵒᵖ, left-module handedness, N ⊗_B M composition and comparison directions agree. Finite coherence is checked with explicit maps; no cocomplete-category realization or simultaneous choice-free splitting is imported.

Ungraded tensor exactness and sum preservation are used on underlying modules. The arbitrary-module comparison is quoted with its hypotheses, then a homogeneous presentation proof is supplied separately; ungraded transformation classification is not applied to unrestricted graded transformations.

The unsigned graded associators and unitors are the same underlying maps as the cited Morita coherence maps. The proof supplies the pseudofunctor comparison in the required direction and checks coherent 2-cells.

Current consumers state the exact finite tensor and dual-kernel Hom classifications, retain agreeing scalars and chosen small module models, and distinguish unconditional essential surjectivity from supplied splitting. The existence theorem explicitly carries AC.

Most interfaces preserve C²/C¹ distinctions, actual collision subsets, topological surface normal forms and local persistence. Exceptions are recorded in alerts: the persistence fact is worded globally, the one-quadrant index count is attributed to the wrong supplier, and two fixed-cap applications omit V's domain extension over the full cap image. The C²-atlas/C¹-defining-form genericity adaptations are explicitly argued rather than silently changing the supplier's Statement.
